$comment: P4.D198 / v4 bcd7e4852 (bug 151) — the tier-1 corpus for `shrinkImageForLlmTransport`. BOTH sides run the SAME per-case SCRIPT below a deterministic encoder: v4 through a `jest.doMock('sharp')` and v5 through `quilltap_harness::ScriptedTranscoder`, so the encoded BYTES are comparable (D19 forbids comparing real sharp against real libwebp). `originalLen` synthesizes the input as `(i * 7 + 13) & 0xff`; a step's encode is `(quality + i) & 0xff` for `len` bytes. `script.metadata` is either {width, height} (either may be null, which is sharp resolving a bag without them) or the string "throws"; `script.final` is what a metadata probe of a NON-original buffer answers. A ladder that asks for a rung the script does not carry is a CORPUS bug and panics loudly on both sides.

cases.label: non_image_mime
cases.note: Arm (1), the `startsWith('image/')` half. Silent, and the codec is never consulted.

cases.label: image_mime_unresizable
cases.note: Arm (1), the `canResizeImage` half — an image mime OUTSIDE RESIZABLE_MIME_TYPES.

cases.label: mime_uppercase_prefix
cases.note: v4's `startsWith('image/')` is case-SENSITIVE while `canResizeImage` lowercases: an uppercase PREFIX fails arm (1) and passes through.

cases.label: mime_mixed_case_subtype
cases.note: The other half of that asymmetry: a mixed-case SUBTYPE passes `startsWith` and is lowercased by `canResizeImage`, so it shrinks — and comes out `image/webp`.

cases.label: small_under_ceiling
cases.note: Arm (4), both conjuncts satisfied: the buffer comes back BY IDENTITY and no encode is attempted.

cases.label: small_over_ceiling_fits_at_65
cases.note: Edge already inside the box but base64 (533,334) over the ceiling, so arm (4) does NOT fire and the ladder runs. Rung 78's encode still misses; rung 65 clears it.

cases.label: oversize_edge_fits_at_first_rung
cases.note: The common production shape: an over-1024 edge means arm (4) cannot fire whatever the byte size, and one rung clears the ceiling.

cases.label: oversize_edge_never_fits
cases.note: Never refuses: all four rungs miss the ceiling and the image goes out at rung 45 — `best` is the LAST rung TRIED, not the smallest possible.

cases.label: grow_discard_small_edge
cases.note: Arm (7), BOTH conjuncts: every rung GREW the payload and the edge was already inside the box, so the re-encode is discarded and the stored mime is kept.

cases.label: grow_but_oversize_edge
cases.note: Arm (7)'s SECOND conjunct, which is the easy one to drop: the encode grew 1,000 bytes to 5,000, and it is STILL taken, because capping a 2048px edge is worth paying bytes for. Mutation M1 targets exactly this row.

cases.label: undecodable_metadata_throws
cases.note: v4's `sharp(buffer).metadata()` REJECTS and the whole `try` lands in the `catch`. v5's `metadata` is infallible, so it answers no dimensions, `longest_edge` is 0, arm (4)'s first conjunct fails and the FIRST `shrink_to_webp` Err produces the warn. Same outcome by a different route — the declared `v5Calls` below IS that difference, and the script makes both sides carry the same `error` bytes.
cases.v5CallsWhy: v4 throws at the metadata probe and never reaches the ladder; v5's probe cannot throw, so the ladder is asked once and refuses. The trait doc (`shrink_to_webp`) records the mapping.

cases.label: encode_throws_at_rung_2
cases.note: The `catch` wraps the WHOLE ladder, so rung 1's perfectly good 600,000-byte encode is discarded along with everything else: stored bytes out, one warn. A partial ladder must never leak its `best`.

cases.label: provider_declares_a_ceiling
cases.note: ANTHROPIC declares `maxBase64Size` 5 MiB, so arm (2)'s `min` reads the registry and the TRANSPORT target wins. The `ceiling` in the log bag is the comparand.

cases.label: provider_without_declared_ceiling
cases.note: OPENROUTER declares `maxBase64Size: null`, so the registry falls back to the 4 MiB DEFAULT — the other registry branch — and the transport target still wins.

cases.label: provider_absent
cases.note: Arm (2)'s `None` branch: this module's budget alone, no registry read. v4's bag carries `provider: undefined`, which `JSON.stringify` DROPS; v5's tracing field renders EMPTY. That is the recorded log narrowing, asserted by name.
